dimension_note: Three arms, one per real entry point. `smoke` is the monitor question — does the thing we deployed still work right now; `hunt` is the unattended search for a regression nobody has reported yet; `verdict` is what happens to a run that already ran, i.e. reading the record, refusing it or turning a finding into an issue. The second axis is how the request arrives; the third is the founder's two languages, since the trigger text is English and the real messages are usually Italian. The failure this corpus is built to catch is theft in the outbound direction: this door claiming a diff that `real-testing` owns, a fix that `bugfix` owns, or a known bug that `issue-contract` owns. All four negatives sit on that boundary, and the fourth sits on the door's own declared refusal — destructive testing against a shared production database.
coverage: 3 arms, 9 positives (three per arm, one per arrival style), 4 negatives. Band 10-20 at 3 declared arms.
